sub_palette: east_asian (japonic) lean + north_american (woodland) substrate (cross-family fusion, Japonic-leaning)

blend.lean_parent: east_asian (japonic: the open CV-mora islands and shrine-vales, the kami of mountain and forest, the rice-and-silk-and-jade staple register, the torii-shrine and the castle-town, clan-first X-no-Y naming, the daimyo houses under the shogun, rendaku voicing, pitch-accent)
blend.substrate_parent: north_american (woodland: the Iroquoian longhouse-confederacy of matrilineal clans, the deep-forest and grove word-stock, the kanata-town/kanonhsa-longhouse/ononta-hill/kahyonha-river roots, the maize-bean-squash-and-maple staple words, the labial-sparse polysynthetic compounds, the forest- and clan-spirits)
blend.lean: East-Asian-heavy (Japonic) - a single fused people of the forested vales, where the shrine-clan of the island-arc and the longhouse-clan of the deep woods grew into one tongue and one rite: the kami and the forest-spirit as one. The Japonic shrine/rule/clan/land register is the backbone; the Woodland forest/longhouse/material/staple words are the substrate. Not a ruling elite over a populace - one merged people, one fused language (per gdd-hybrid-conlang-fusion.md).

_note: NEW cross-family hybrid under the base/hybrid model. BASE_08 (Japonic, Yamataian register) x BASE_11 (Woodland, Oronan/Iroquoian register). FUSION-FIRST (gdd-hybrid-conlang-fusion.md): a SINGLE fused tongue, one word per concept, derived by principled sound-change from both parents - not a slash-pair dual-register gloss. CIV/CLAN DECIDED by inheritance: Japanese (East-Asian) base = Civilized, Woodland (Amerindian) base = Clanhold, and any Civ parent -> Civ, so Maniwa is Civilized (feudal). Concept: the shrine and the longhouse, the kami and the forest-spirit, the island-clan and the forest-clan grown into a single rite over the forested vales of a temperate woodland-realm (a Japonic-Woodland fusion; 'Maniwa', the true-forest realm). Lean = Japonic (the rule/shrine/clan/kin/land register, the X-no-Y clan-first naming, the rendaku CV-mora phonology, the daimyo-under-shogun ladder); substrate = Woodland (forest, longhouse, grove, maize, maple, fur, flint - the forest, dwelling, material and staple words). Common-word lexicon and rank titles use the real Japanese register (allowed, catalog 5.3), with the Woodland substrate words fused into Japonic phonology (the labial-sparse polysynthetic Iroquoian compounds truncated and CV-moraized); DEITY names are morphs of the Agrippan canon - Japonic native-kami canon-morphs PRIMARY (the yamataian column: Terashi-no-kami, Hagane-no-kami, Iwane-no-kami, Amatsukaze-no-kami, Megumi-hime, Takami-no-kami), Woodland morphs SECONDARY (the oronan / family_north_american.json theonym_sets.woodland column, softened to Japonic CV shape), never real Shinto kami or Iroquois gods. All three alignments (per 2026-06-27: all human cultures allow Lawful/Neutral/Chaotic). Ruler/domain DISPLAY titles are ENGLISH except the kingdom which uses the approved commonly-known term 'Shogun' (the military overlord of the realm) and the duchy which uses 'Daimyo' (the great clan-house lord); conlang titles in ruler_native/domain_native (Japonic-lean fused) for NPC dialogue. CSV phonetic profile 'Ejective consonants with soft consonants'; grammar 'SOV, Polysynthetic honorifics'.

phonology.palette: East-Asian (Japonic) lean - open CV moras (only coda -n), five vowels a i u e o, pitch-accent, no consonant clusters, rendaku (sequential voicing) in compounds, clan-first X-no-Y, kami honorifics -no-kami/-no-mikoto/-hime - taking up a North-American (Woodland/Iroquoian) substrate: the labial-sparse consonant stock (t k s h n r w y, ts, kw), glottalized/ejective seams softened, long polysynthetic forest-and-longhouse compounds, the maize/maple/fur/flint word-stock, nasal vowels resolved. Per the CSV: ejective consonants with soft consonants (the Woodland glottalized t'/k' and kw-clusters audible as a hardened onset beneath the Japonic CV gentleness, the ejective seam softened into a geminate or a plain stop before the open mora); grammar is SOV with polysynthetic honorifics (the Japonic SOV verb-final order carrying the Woodland polysynthetic incorporation as stacked honorific -no-/-ke/-shi affixes). Theophoric on the Japonic kami-morphs (Terashi-, Hagane-) with the Woodland forest-spirit morphs as the grove register (Tarano-, Kayano-).
phonology.phonotactics: open CV moras with only coda -n (Japonic); Woodland CV(C) roots shed their glottal stops and nasal-vowel codas and breathe their final consonant out into an open Japonic mora or geminate at the seam (kanata>kanata/kanta, ononta>ononta>onota, kahyonha>kayowa, karhakonha>karako, kanonhsa>kanosa); the long Iroquoian polysynthetic compound is truncated to two or three moras and welded vowel-final; clusters dissolve (kw>k/ku, hr>r, tsy>chi); rendaku voicing on the second element; -no-/-ke/-shi linking; -yama/-mori/-machi/-gawa over the Woodland kanata-/karako-/onota- forest-and-town elements; pitch-accent (the Japonic pattern overrides Woodland stress).

sound_changes: Woodland labial-sparse polysynthetic compounds adapt to the Japonic CV-mora shape: the long Iroquoian stem is truncated to two or three moras and breathed vowel-final or to a coda -n, glottal stops and nasal-vowel codas dropped (kanata>kanta, ononta>onota, kahyonha>kayowa, karhakonha>karako, kanonhsa>kanosa, oskenonton>oskeno)

Woodland glottalized/ejective onsets and the kw/hr/tsy clusters soften toward the Japonic inventory: the ejective seam becomes a geminate or a plain stop before the open mora (t'>tt/t, k'>kk/k), kw>k/ku, hr>r, tsy>chi; Woodland has no labials and Japonic supplies none new, so the fused stock stays labial-light except where a Japonic root carries m/b

Woodland stress is overridden by Japonic pitch-accent; word order is Japonic SOV; the Iroquoian polysynthetic incorporation is kept as stacked honorific affixes reshaped to Japonic -no-/-ke/-shi (the X-of-Y forest-compound > X-no-Y)

the Japonic five vowels a i u e o with rendaku voicing dominate; Woodland nasal vowels (en/on) resolve to plain e/o or e-n/o-n; retain the Japonic open-mora color and the audible Woodland forest-roots (kanata-, karako-, onota-, wahta-) softened to CV shape; rendaku voices the second element of a compound (kanta>-ganta, mori>-mori)

very short Woodland roots take a Japonic open mora to reach a CV(C) vowel-final shape (ase>ase, ohaha>ohawa, owera>owera, atste>atse); a stem that would end in a bare consonant gains an echo vowel or a coda -n
fusion_rules.source_tilt: forest/longhouse/grove/material/staple words from Woodland roots (the substrate forest and its making - karhakonha forest, kanonhsa longhouse, onenhste maize, wahta maple, kahonwa fur, onenhia flint), then filtered to Japonic phonology; kin-line/shrine/rule/land/water/quality/abstract/war words from Japonic roots (the lean register - kawa, yama, umi, uji, jinja, shiro, imi, kuro); every chosen root then run through the one Japonic-shaped sound-law (CV-mora truncation, ejective-seam softening, rendaku) so the split is invisible at the surface

lexicon._note: Single fused tongue derived via phonology.fusion_rules (gdd-hybrid-conlang-fusion.md): Woodland forest/longhouse/material/staple roots + Japonic shrine/rule/kin/land/water roots, all run through one Japonic-shaped sound-law (Iroquoian polysynthetic compounds truncated to CV moras, ejective seams softened, nasal vowels resolved, rendaku voicing); portmanteaus mark the blended institutions and bloodline. One word per concept, no slashes.

toponymic_suffixes: Kan- / Kano- (longhouse-town; from Woodland kanata/kanonhsa, truncated)
Kara- / Mori- (forest-/wood-; from Woodland karhakonha + Japonic mori)
morphology.patronymic_form: the Japonic clan-first order leads (uji / -shi precedes the given name, -no- links X no Y, the noble house takes -ke); the Woodland substrate keeps its matrilineal clan-totem as the uji-totem and the clan-mother's bestowal-rite, reshaped so the totem-clan name carries a -no- honorific link. The throne fuses both - a daimyo-house that is also a matrilineal totem-clan, the name held and bestowed within the clan but ordered father-line at the crown.
morphology.compounding_rule: [clan] no [given] in the Japonic manner; toponyms = feature/quality + type, the Woodland forest-and-longhouse element truncated and welded vowel-final: Kuro-yama (black-mountain), Kara-mori (the deep-forest), Kano-machi (the longhouse-town), rendaku voicing (kawa>-gawa, kanta>-ganta). Quality + feature lead the compound: oo (great), kuro (black), kari-imi (sacred).

title_ladder.government: feudal (a fused shrine-and-longhouse realm: the Shogun and the great daimyo clan-houses over the forested vales, the shugo-governors over the kanmachi longhouse-towns, the totem-clans and their clan-mothers sworn beneath; the kannushi shrine-keepers and the rotihontsa faithkeepers serve the one kami-and-forest rite together; the Tenno reigns in name)
title_ladder._tiers_note: Japonic-lean fused ladder, ascending; the native forms blend the Japonic clanhold titles (jito/shugo/daimyo/shogun/tenno) with the Woodland sachem-and-firekeeper register (royaner/hoyaneh/tadodaho), the Woodland element softened to CV shape. Jitoroyan (estate-lord + sachem) barony; Shugoraka (border-deputy + war-chief) march; Shugoyane (province-governor + peace-chief) county; Daimyoken (great clan-house lord) duchy; Kokushiyo (province-master) principality; Shogun (military overlord, the Bakufu) kingdom; Tennotado (heavenly sovereign + presiding firekeeper) empire over Tenka. The Tenno reigns in name, the Shogun and the daimyo houses rule in fact; the matrilineal totem-clans keep their clan-mothers beneath the crown. DISPLAY titles are English except the kingdom which uses the approved commonly-known term 'Shogun' (set in 'ruler', its native form also Shogun) and the duchy which uses 'Daimyo' (the great clan-house lord, its native form Daimyoken). The kannushi shrine-priest and the rotihontsa faithkeeper stand outside the ladder. (Rank native-forms fuse the real Japanese/Iroquois register, allowed.)
title_ladder.heir: Yotsugi-ase (the designated heir-son, the newly-raised; the title is conferred father-line at the crown but bestowed within the totem-clan beneath)

honorifics.elder: Thototsu (the eldest / elder, from Woodland thotiron softened)

vassalage.fealty: Chugiwenta (the loyal covenant, from Japonic chugi + Woodland kaswentha)
vassalage.tribute: Nenguatse (the render-gift, from Japonic nengu + Woodland atste)

title_ladder.display_policy: Ruler/domain titles shown in setting-gen, domain lists and vassal trees are ENGLISH, except the kingdom which uses the approved commonly-known term 'Shogun' (the military overlord) and the duchy which uses 'Daimyo' (the great clan-house lord). The *_native conlang (Japonic-lean fused) forms are for NPC DIALOGUE ONLY, never for structural/UI displays.

people_name_convention.order: clan/house name (the uji-totem) first, then given name; the Japonic -no- links clan and name (X no Y); the totem-clan is matrilineal in the Woodland manner (the clan-mother holds and bestows the name) but the daimyo-house orders its succession father-line; a gen-puku adult name for warriors; order family-first.
surname_source: uji-totem clan (matrilineal, by animal-totem; the Woodland ohwachira reshaped to the Japonic clan-first uji)
people_name_convention.dual_register: the buke (warrior daimyo-houses) carry a totem-clan name + court/military title; commoners use a single clan-totem name or trade-name; the clan-mother bestows and may recall the personal name.
people_name_convention.theophoric: names invoke the kami and the forest-spirits + an element: -maru (child/blade), Take- (valor), Kami- (divine), Mori- (forest), Kara- (deep-wood): e.g. Takebimaru, Morikari, names honoring Terashi-no-kami and the forest-power Tarano.

religion._note: Deity-names are morphs of the Agrippan canon - Japonic native-kami canon-morphs PRIMARY (family_east_asian.json theonym_sets.japonic, the yamataian column: Terashi-no-kami, Hagane-no-kami, Iwane-no-kami, Amatsukaze-no-kami, Megumi-hime, Takami-no-kami), Woodland morphs SECONDARY (family_north_american.json theonym_sets.woodland, the oronan column, softened to Japonic CV shape), never real Shinto kami or Iroquois gods. The fused rite identifies the shrine-kami and the forest-spirit as one face - the kami and the forest-spirit as one: the kannushi of the torii and the rotihontsa faithkeeper of the rite-longhouse keep the same powers. All three alignments; the kami pervade all things, the forest- and clan-spirits dwell in the deep wood, and the ancestral dead are honored at the household shrine and the burial-grove.
religion.the_one: Takami-no-kami (Japonic; Woodland grove-name Terano-Aterhon) - the High-Heaven One, distant above the myriad kami and forest-spirits, honored not petitioned; revered when Lawful, set aside when Neutral

Tulrius.gloss: the Shining One, sun and right-rule, the day-keeper; Lawful power

Orlandus.gloss: the Steel One, the blade-oath and war

Gaiandus.gloss: the Rock-Root, the enduring mountain and forest-earth

Realta.gloss: the Mercy-Maiden, mother and the life-giving clan-mother of the powers

worship_by_alignment.Lawful: venerates the Lawful powers - Takami-no-kami, Terashi-no-kami the just sun, Hagane-no-kami of the sworn blade, Megumi-hime the merciful - at the torii-shrine and the rite-longhouse alike, and names the Chaotic powers oni (devouring spirits) or the wild aramitama, warded; the ordered warrior-way and the council's peace bind together
worship_by_alignment.Neutral: the ancestral dead (the senzo enshrined at the household jinja and the akhsosenzo of the burial-grove) and the forest- and clan-spirits of the deep wood and the longhouse; the great powers invoked at the torii and the grove situationally, somewhat honored and somewhat feared; the thanksgivings to the growing things kept by the council-calendar
worship_by_alignment.Chaotic: Venerates the Chaotic powers of the canon - the war-flame and the storm-kami, the devouring void and the mountain-oni - and names the Lawful powers, and Takami-no-kami, as the tyrant-kami to be defied.

religion.demon_epithet_pattern: the Chaotic powers, warded as oni / the wild aramitama (Japonic) or the demonized forest-spirits (Woodland), keep their morphs + an epithet: Maraxus -> Takebi-no-kami the War-Flame (Woodland Warakso the War-Fire); Vacidus -> Utsuro-no-kami the Devouring Void (Woodland Wasido the Devourer); Lusanto -> Kogane-Orochi the gold hoard-serpent (Woodland Rusano the Greed-Serpent).

clergy_ladder.9: Saishu (high priest of the realm) / Kanoyonitha (the council's high keeper)

religion.religious_orders_pattern: the Jinja (torii-shrine) or the Kanomachi-rite-longhouse (the kanonhses of the Woodland substrate) of [power]: 'the Jinja of Terashi-no-kami', 'the rite-longhouse of Tarano', within its torii, sacred grove and thanksgiving-circle.
religion.saints_pattern: great ancestors and fallen heroes enshrined as kami (the eirei, honored dead) at the clan jinja, and the founders of the council's peace and the honored clan-mothers kept in the council's recital; honored at the shrine, the rite-longhouse and the burial-grove; 'the kami [name]'.

holy_symbol_motifs.Terashi-no-kami: a rising sun-disc above a mirror and sword, set over the longhouse
holy_symbol_motifs.Hagane-no-kami: a bare blade crossed before a torii and the council-fire
holy_symbol_motifs.Iwane-no-kami: a great oak rooted deep beneath the grey peak
